newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil gov't sees 11 new hydro tenders by yr-end.
newsitem.headline: Brazil gov't sees 11 new hydro tenders by yr-end.

text.p: Tenders for the private construction and operation of 11 new Brazilian hydroelectric projects should be published by the end of the year, a spokeswoman for the Mines and Energy Ministry said.
The 11 projects would produce a total of 2,300 megawatts of power and require total investment of $2.5 billion, all of which would come from the private sector, the spokeswoman said.
A meeting of the National Privatization Council scheduled for Thursday will receive a formal request from the ministry that the projects be included in Brazil's privatization program, she said.
The largest of the 11 projects is Campos Novos, an 880-megawatt installation in Santa Catarina state, followed by the 450-megawatt Cana Brava in Goias and the 372-megawatt Irape in Minas Gerais.
Brazil began offering new hydroelectric projects to the private sector earlier this year.

Of the four so far included in the program -- totalling 260 megawatts -- two have been awarded to private groups, one is currently in a phase for the receiving of bids and another failed to receive any offers.

As well as new hydro projects, the Brazilian government is offering to the private sector 22 units begun but left uncompleted by the public sector. They would generate a total of 7,300 megawatts, requiring $5.6 billion in new investment.
